events.name: Counterfeit Leftovers
events.intro: A folding table of half-eaten apples, glossy as toys. Jinty, the seller, grins wide. "Genuine Leftovers, only ₽300!" They shine like plastic. The hand-written label reads "Lefttovers".

success.text: You pay. Jinty wraps it in newspaper, very fast. At the next bend you unwrap it. It squeaks. It is a dog toy, painted red. Jinty and the table are gone.

"Two Ts," you say, loud enough to carry. Jinty looks at the label. The crowd looks at the label. Jinty looks at the crowd, and runs. Somebody starts clapping, and then everybody is, and someone passes a hat for you.
You lean in and sniff. Real Leftovers smell of apple and a little of soil. These smell of nothing at all. Jinty sees your face change and starts, very casually, to pack up.

remembers.notice: You already know these smell of nothing. Only one thing left to say, and the label is right there.

events.name: The Fake Nurse
events.intro: A man in a nurse's pink cap waves you over. "Tired team? Hand me their Balls, I'll fix them right up!" His smile is off. No Chansey, no Audino. His cap badge is printed paper.

success.text: He takes them behind a curtain. Real healing light flickers. He comes back with your team, healthy, and a bill for ₽500. A real Pokémon Center has never charged a coin. He is gone before you finish reading it.
He blinks. "Day off." He blinks again. "Sick. Day off for being sick." He straightens the paper badge on his cap, which only draws your eye to it.

You flick the badge. It bends. He looks at it, then at you, and the whole act sags. "It's my first week," he mutters. A grunt in training. He drops a Potion as he bolts, which is honestly very nurse-like of him.

remembers.notice: "Day off," he said. The paper badge on his cap is still curling at one corner.

events.name: The Pickpocket
events.intro: A shoulder hits yours in the crowd. "Sorry, sorry!" A hand was in your bag, and now it is not, and neither is the best thing that was in there. A figure is already running.

success.text: You run. Through a market, over a wall, round three corners and into a dead end. The thief turns, panting, and hands it back without a word. It took the rest of the afternoon.
Your fastest Pokémon is gone before you finish pointing. It is back before the thief has finished running, carrying your things in its mouth, very proud.
You let it go. Things are only things. But you will remember the face, and somewhere, in some vault, your things will be waiting with a label on them.

events.name: The Disguised Merchant
events.intro: A friendly seller with prices a little too good. Three Great Balls for ₽300. A radio on his belt hisses softly. His boots are black, polished, and standard issue for a certain team.

success.text: The Balls are real, and cheap, and you know exactly where your money just went. Somewhere a plan you would rather stop moves a little faster.
"Nice boots," you say. "Team issue?" His smile drops like a shutter. The radio on his belt barks a name and a place before he can switch it off. You heard it. He knows you heard it.

choices.label: Ask where the goods came from.

success.text: "Here and there," he says, too quickly. His eyes go to his own boots, just for a second, the way people look at the thing they hope you will not.

remembers.notice: "Here and there," he said. He keeps shifting his feet, as if the boots were too tight.

events.name: The Poké Ball Sting
events.intro: A man in a trench coat sells "special" Poké Balls from the back of a van. No maker's mark on any of them. Three more men sit in the van. One Ball on the tray rattles by itself.

success.text: ₽1,000 for a bag of shining Balls. The first one you throw cracks in half in the air. So does the second. The van, of course, is long gone.
You pop it open before he can stop you. A tiny, frightened Pokémon tumbles out, someone's, with a name tag. The man runs. You carry it to the Lost and Found, and its trainer cries when they see it.
Crates. Dozens of them, stamped with ports you know, all rattling. This is no stall. It is a ring. The three men climb out, one at a time, cracking their knuckles.

events.name: The Bake Sale
events.intro: A cheerful stall of cookies "for sick Pokémon". The cash box names no charity. The cashier's collar has a red R stitched on it. One cookie, under a little glass dome, is labelled "Boss's".

success.text: ₽200. It is, annoyingly, a very good cookie. Your lead gets half and perks right up. Somewhere, the money is counted in a back room by people in black.
"Um." The cashier looks at the cash box. "The... Pokémon one." He tugs his collar up higher, which puts the R right under your nose.
"That's an R," you say. The cashier, Petey, bursts into tears. "I just like baking!" He gives you a cookie for free, and a recipe, and his whole sad story. You believe every word of it.

remembers.notice: The other cashier looks very familiar. Dilly, from Grunt School, sees you and ducks under the table.

success.text: "That's an R," you say. Petey bursts into tears. "I just like baking!" Under the table, Dilly whispers, "Don't tell them I was here." Petey gives you a cookie for free.

remembers.notice: "The... Pokémon one," he said. The R on his collar has not gone anywhere.

events.name: The Shady Surveyor
events.intro: Four people at a market stall. One of them just lifted a wallet; you saw it, not clearly. One has dirt on his knees. One wears a team pin. One keeps a hand in a pocket. One is the victim.

choices.label: Accuse the one with a pin.

success.text: You point. The pin-wearer freezes, then empties his coat on the stall. The wallet falls out. Its owner hugs you, then hugs the stallholder, then tips you for your trouble.

choices.label: Accuse the one with a hand in their pocket.

success.text: She takes her hand out. It is empty and very cold. "It's winter," she says, icily. The whole stall stares at you. You stare at the floor.

choices.label: Accuse the one with dirt on their knees.

success.text: "I'm a gardener," he says, wounded, and shows you a trowel. He has been kneeling in begonias all morning. He forgives you quickly, which somehow makes it worse.

choices.label: Tell the victim to check their pocket.

success.text: The victim pats his coat. "My wallet!" The pin-wearer bolts at once, which answers everything. You give chase through the stalls, and he turns at the end of the row to fight.

events.name: Galactic Energy Corp. Booth
events.intro: A friendly booth under a striped awning, a banner reading Galactic Energy Corp., a stack of glossy flyers. The smiling clerk wears a scarf, and under the scarf, just for a second, a pin you have seen before. "Clean energy from space! Well. From a lake. Sign up for our newsletter?" He asks which way you are headed.

success.text: You write your name, and, because he asks so nicely, your route. He beams. "Wonderful! We'll be in touch." Behind the booth, a radio crackles once and goes quiet.

Under the glossy photos, in type so small it is nearly a line: "Galactic Energy Corp., a wholly owned holding of" and then a name nobody would ever look twice at. You will look twice. It is a thread, and threads lead somewhere.

"Nice pin," you say. The smile stays on his face for one more second, out of habit. Then it drops, and so does the act. "Should've worn a thicker scarf." He kicks the flyers aside and reaches for a Poké Ball.

win.text: Exposed the Galactic Energy Corp. booth. It folded before nightfall.

remembers.intro: A friendly booth under a striped awning, a banner reading Galactic Energy Corp., a stack of glossy flyers. The smiling clerk keeps his arms folded. When he reaches for a flyer, the inside of his sleeve flashes a pin you have seen before. They have learned to hide it. Not well enough. "Clean energy from space! Well. From a lake. Sign up for our newsletter?" He asks which way you are headed.
remembers.notice: You have already read the small print. Galactic Energy Corp. is a front, and you know the name of the shell behind it.

events.name: Officer Jenny
events.intro: Officer Jenny arrives as the booth comes down, notebook already out. She takes your statement and the flyers, and nods at you like one professional to another. "Good eye. Keep it open."

success.text: You salute. She salutes back, crisply, and climbs onto her motorbike. "If you see another one," she calls, "you know where I am."

remembers.notice: Officer Jenny closes her notebook. "Three fronts. Three." She unpins something from her own jacket. "We give these out maybe twice a year."

success.text: A Detective's Badge, small and bright, still warm from her jacket. "They'll change their tells now," she warns. "Pins in sleeves, probably. Keep looking." You pin it on.

effects.text: Officer Jenny pinned a Detective's Badge on you after three front booths fell.
